The pure event-notice shim
==========================

The queue stores the notice as a USER-INPUT text item, not as a data item, so
data-not-instruction is a convention of the strict shapes, the fixed template
and the chat's own rule, never a property of the queue; the boundary is
behavioural. The source line is a hint, not authentication.

The event id appears once in the template text; that is a property of the text,
not a count of anything the chat did. The receipt counts user-input items, not
mentions.

This is a text queue with staged evidence from two sources (the queue call and
the chat's own session record), not a structured event bus.

STARTED, FINISHED and HEARD are observed, separate receipts. Each names its
source, identifier and timestamp; each is unknown when the evidence is missing
or the read window closed. The started observer reports at most one input item
observed per event id: zero is unknown, one is started, two or more is unproven
with the count. FINISHED is the next assistant message after the item, whether
or not that message names the event id. HEARD is a person's word or playback
telemetry and is unknown by default.

The queue confirms queued only; no other stage is inferred from the queue call.
Dedupe reduces repeats through a bounded journal; an evicted id is queued again.

A value outside the schema is refused before the queue call. An event that
carries an unknown key is refused with a reason naming the key, and free event
text never becomes an instruction.

Rehearsal facts (a synthetic event, one Codex thread, closed): an idle chat took
the strict-template notice as one user-input item and answered in about 4 s; a
busy chat held the item in the queue and drained it after the turn as one
user-input item; a free-form event is not a template result and is never cited
as one; the closed chat was not tested for real, because the shim refuses it by
its own thread check.

The live driver is reviewed code under herdr/test/fixtures/, not a line first
seen in a runbook. It is a dry run by default; LIVE=1 spawns the queue argv
array without a shell. Its sha256 is quoted by the runbook.
